**Ready for the maintainer to merge, once #2054 has merged first** (this PR is stacked on it).

## What looks good
- `every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy` (`crates/app/tests/holder_reference.rs:119`) loops `holder_library::library()`, which is every entry. Each entry runs at its default and at a shifted gauge length and projection, both picked and assumed (`machine_default`), and again after save and load. The compared string holds the judged tool, the profile, the band stack, the digest and the facets. The test also asserts that at least 160 comparisons ran, so a shrunken loop would fail. The reference is checked against `old_copy`, which is built from `HolderEntry::points`, the same call the old pick used.
- The older-file case is pinned: a v61 project with a drawn copy and a plain holder cylinder loads with the same reads, operation status and warnings, and the BT30 flange hits the fixture wall hit for hit. Older tool libraries load as custom holders.
- An unknown entry refuses the file by tool name, in the project and in `.camtools`, and no other holder lands (`build_library`, `crates/app/src/tool_body.rs:155`). A grouped pick, bad lengths and `holder` beside `body` are refused by name too.
- No path swaps a holder silently:
  - `edit_tool` refuses a `holder` patch (`crates/app/src/mcp/tool_edit.rs:16`).
  - `add_tool` refuses a `holder` reference inside `definition` (`crates/app/src/mcp/edit.rs:174`).
  - Apply in the profile editor goes through `SetToolBody::library`. An unchanged outline keeps the reference, and an edited point makes it a custom profile in one undo step.
  - `.camtools` import goes through `build_library`.
- The "no bump" claim holds against main. `PROJECT_VERSION` is 61 at v0.21.0 and 62 on main (unreleased, from c51f5541b). The `.camtools` `VERSION` is 1 at v0.21.0, and main already adds `LEFT_HAND_VERSION = 2`. The PR reuses it as `HOLDER_REF_VERSION = 2` (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs:45`).
- There is a decision entry, no new dependency line, no snapshot PNG change, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, and the body ends `Fixes #2016` with a `Changelog:` line and `BREAKING CHANGE:`.

## Results (locally on m5, trial-merged with upstream/main a277dd9d5; the runner was not used)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-tools --lib` | 87 passed |
| app: `holder_reference` 7, `holder_library` 12, `tool_library_holders` 8, `mcp_holder` 5, `mcp_edit_tool` 3, `machine_default_holder` 13, `tool_body` 12, `tool_body_judged` 8, `tool_body_view` 7, `tool_library` 14, `project_roundtrip` 73, `sim_tool_body` 7, `turning_holder` 8, `commands_undo` 30, `tool_after_state` 5, `vendor_tool_body` 3 | all passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 862 passed, 6 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the full gate-mapped list, which is wide because the stack carries #2054. I did not run the pixel snapshots. Windows and Linux are not exercised.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Notes (not blocking)
1. `PROCESS_VERSION` goes from 76 to 77 (`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`) and the `camcraft-mcp` skill is changed. This collides with open PRs #2083 and #1738, which also bump it. Whichever merges later takes the next number when it merges main.
2. The stack makes every `.camtools` version 2 file ambiguous. A development build of main that reads a version 2 file with a `holder` key may drop the key without refusing, so the tool would load with no holder and collision would be judged without it. The PR body notes this for projects (v62). The same applies to `.camtools`, and it only affects development builds, since v0.21.0 refuses version 2.
3. A corrected library entry now reaches every project that names it, where a copy kept the old numbers. The author documents this, and it is the point of the change.
4. The test's older files are this build's own files rewritten to the old form. No real v0.21.0 file was read, and the PR body says so.
5. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests.rs` (5318 lines) is already over the file-size limit and grows slightly.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
